When adding exemptions to secret-scanning tools (e.g., gitleaks allowlists) for known false positives such as synthetic test IDs or sample tokens, scope the exemption as narrowly as possible using precise match conditions (e.g., condition = AND combined with regexTarget = match) rather than broad path- or pattern-based exclusions. A loosely scoped allowlist can accidentally suppress detection of real secrets located near the false positive. After adding any exemption, verify both that the intended false positives are ignored and that a genuine secret placed in the same file/path is still flagged, confirming the scanner's coverage remains intact.
